pillars.note: Two stated objectives: material flammability in microgravity (prevention) and the effectiveness of an extinguishing agent (suppression). Pillar is the curator's classification, not a source statement.

evidence.quote: Begin to bridge the gap between the normal gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test#1 method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity.
Assess the effectiveness of an inert, gaseous extinguishing agent (similar to that used on ISS) in putting out flames over different materials, geometries, preheating, and flow.

hardware.value: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with a 76 mm x 76 mm flow duct, on the ISS
hardware.note: The ISA-Tab says airflow up to 40 cm/s; the requirements document plans 5 to 50 cm/s (SRD p. 4). Not reconciled.

evidence.quote: The experiment was conducted aboard the International Space Station (ISS)
The samples were placed in a small flow duct (76 mm x 76 mm cross section)
airflow speeds reaching as high as 40 cm/s
The airflow speed can be adjusted from 5 to
50 cm/s. Nitrogen is supplied through the nozzle

nominal_atmosphere.note: Pressure only (1 atm = 14.6959 psi), taken from slide captions of individual tests; no section states it as a nominal condition for the whole investigation. O2 is not set: the experimental table has no O2 column and the slides show different values (17% in these captions, 22% on p. 31). Do not assume cabin air.

evidence.quote: Atmosphere: 17% O2/N2; 1 atm; Flow speed: 12 cm/s (left to right)
